description:
The Energy Community UI as a self-contained deployment of the MANAGEMENT tenant
(AB#3683).

Install this on the management tenant only. One Helm release serves every
operating tenant below it: the app reads the tenant from its `/:tenantId` route
and offers the management tenant's CHILD tenants in the switcher. The management
tenant itself is never a UI destination — `available-tenants.service.ts` excludes
`rootTenantId` explicitly.

Seeds the two entities that make the management tenant self-contained:

1. `System.Identity/Client` — the `energy-community-app` OIDC client, with the
   deployment's own URLs and `AutoProvisionInChildTenants: true`, so every child
   tenant gets a mirror instead of an operator adding redirect URIs by hand in
   each one. Clients are per-tenant records, and a single shared host does not
   change that: without the mirror, sign-in against a child tenant fails with
   `Invalid redirect_uri` even though the app is configured correctly.

2. `System.Communication/Application` — the Helm deployment, with URLs derived
   from the same placeholders the client uses, and `rootTenantId` bound to
   `{{context.tenantId}}` so the app authenticates against the tenant it is
   installed on.

DELIBERATELY NOT SEEDED

The `DeploymentSite` (670…001, `Pool` before System.Communication 4.0.0) and the
Mesh Adapter (670…002) belong to the service-managed System.Communication blueprint
and reappear on every `EnableCommunication` — a Communication-enabled tenant always
has them, so seeding one here would fight the service for ownership. The Application
associates to the existing DeploymentSite instead (role `Hosts`).

RELATION TO EnergyCommunity.Base

Base stopped seeding a per-tenant Application in 2.3.0: an operating tenant
holds no app workload any more, the app host serves it. Tenants installed
from an older Base still carry that Application (rtId
6a1f14de0b5979da7108457e, hostname
`energy-community-${octo.tenantId}.{{domain.DEFAULT}}`). This blueprint uses
a DIFFERENT rtId so the two never fight over one entity: whichever ran last
would otherwise own it, and uninstalling either would erase everything
carrying its `rtBlueprintSource` — on a productive tenant, the live UI.

MIGRATING A TENANT INSTALLED FROM BASE < 2.3.0 (reversible until step 3)
1. Install this blueprint on the management tenant and deploy its workload.
   Re-parent the tenant below it and verify the client mirror reached it
   (Identity > Clients on the child, or `clients/{id}/mirrors` on the
   management tenant; `ProvisionClientInExistingTenants` backfills).
2. Move the users. Until then the per-tenant deployment keeps serving them.
3. Undeploy the per-tenant workload (`UndeployWorkload -id
   6a1f14de0b5979da7108457e`) AND delete the entity. The CD line guard keys
   on this blueprint (AB#3683): a tenant that still carries the chart but has
   no EnergyCommunity.App installation is skipped with a warning on every run.

VERSION LINE

The MAJOR of this blueprint follows the app's release line, like the other
EnergyCommunity blueprints: the CD only rolls a chart whose MAJOR equals the
MAJOR of the App blueprint installed on the app host. 2.0.0 is the 2.x line
(r2.x tags on main); 1.0.0 was the first publication and is skipped by every
2.x roll — update app hosts with `UpdateBlueprint -tv EnergyCommunity.App-2.0.0`
(System.Communication 3.x) or `EnergyCommunity.App-2.1.0` (4.x, see below).

Hostname/Values/ChartVersion/IngressEnabled are `isRuntimeState` since
System.Communication 3.28 (AB#4706), so the seed values apply on fresh installs
only and a re-apply never overwrites what the operator set in Studio.

2.0.0 -> 2.1.0 (AB#5528, System.Communication 4.x line): the seed associates the Application
with System.Communication/Hosts-1 -> DeploymentSite-1 (was Manages-1 -> Pool-1; renamed in
System.Communication 4.0.0, AB#4924) and pins System.Communication-[4.5,5.0) - 4.5.0 is the
first 4.x any catalog holds. The two shapes cannot share one seed, so 2.1.0 installs ONLY on a
tenant already migrated to 4.x and 2.0.0 stays the 3.x version. MINOR, not major: the MAJOR of
this blueprint is the CD line guard (it must equal the chart MAJOR, AB#4705), and a 3.0.0 would
make every app roll skip the app host. Fixes for 3.x app hosts stay on 2.0.x. Order per app
host: tenant migration to System.Communication 4.x first, then
`UpdateBlueprint -tv EnergyCommunity.App-2.1.0 -m Merge`. The migration already rewrote the
stored edge (RenameAssociationRole / ChangeCkType), so the update is a no-op on the data.
